newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Peregrine Inv to privatise Kwong Sang Hong.
newsitem.headline: Peregrine Inv to privatise Kwong Sang Hong.

text.p: Peregrine Investments Holdings Ltd said it will privatise its Kwong Sang Hong International Ltd unit.
It said it will offer 200 Peregrine shares plus HK$1,700 cash for every 1,000 Kwong Sang Hong shares.

The proposal values the entire issued share capital of Kwong Sang Hong at HK$2.64 billion, or HK$4.35 per share, representing a premium of 34.9 percent over Monday's closing price of HK$3.225, Peregrine said in a statement on Wednesday.
Trading in Kwong Sang Hong and Peregrine shares was due to resume on Wednesday after being suspended on Tuesday.
Peregrine, which owns about 51.9 percent of the issued share capital of Kwong Sang Hong, said it would issue about 64.87 million new shares under the proposal.
The company said if all conditions were fulfilled, the scheme was expected to become effective in March 1997.
Hong Kong-based investment bank Peregrine said the proposal would result in a withdrawal of the listing of Kwong Sang Hong on the Hong Kong stock exchange.

It said the proposal was made because "the market does not consider that KSH is a first tier Hong Kong-listed property company" and the shares would continue to trade at a substantial discount to their net asset value.
The net asset value of the property investment and cosmetic making company was about HK$2.52 billion, or a 22 percent discount to its market capitalisation on December 16.

Peregrine said the current shareholding structure of Kwong Sang Hong, which involves a substantial number of minority shareholders, "has the effect, in practice, of limiting the scope of cooperation possible between the two companies".

It said existing arrangements between the companies may also result "in a lack of clarity for investors as to the respective activities of both companies in the areas of property investment and development".
